prompt:
Style references only: the attached images set the painting style, the colours and the mood. Do not copy their content. Paint it as a concept artist's painted sketch sheet for a cozy, bright strategy game: loose hand-painted brushwork with visible strokes, soft painted light from a warm sunny afternoon coming from the front right, cheerful bright colours, a warm light cream paper background with a soft painted shadow under each object. It is a painting, not a 3D render, not low poly, not a game screenshot. Cozy and friendly like a storybook toy, never grim. No people, no text, no labels, no numbers, no letters, no watermark.

The fourth attached image shows the three guns this game already has, small to large. The new gun belongs to their family: the same painting style, the same dark iron grey, the same chunky rivets and iron bands. Never copy those three guns.

The sheet shows three different designs for one new gun, side by side from left to right, each in a three-quarter view from slightly above, with empty cream paper between them. The new gun is an anti-air gun of the early industrial age that shoots flying cannonballs out of the sky: several thin iron barrels side by side, all pointing steeply up at the sky. The barrels sit together in one compact cradle, and the cradle sits on top of a short round pedestal like a ball on a post, so the whole cradle can swivel and tilt as one piece, with no arms or frame beside it that it could hit. The pedestal stands on a round iron turning mount. It must never read as an ordinary cannon that shoots at walls: thin barrels, several of them, pointing at the sky. No wheels anywhere. No platform, slab or tile under it. Dark iron grey is the main colour. Chunky simple shapes with few big parts, friendly and toy-like. Left: a twin gun, two long thin barrels side by side in a boxy riveted iron cradle. Middle: a quad gun, four thin barrels in a square bundle held together by two thick iron bands in a round drum-shaped cradle. Right: a rotary volley gun, six thin barrels in a ring around a central axle with a round iron plate at the muzzle end and a crank at the back.
